author: GamingBolt
description:
In its current state, Dreadmoor isn’t an easy game to recommend. Its stronger points, like its excellent art direction and addictive core gameplay loop, have already been done better elsewhere, and its narrative is still too far from complete to offer a satisfying experience on its own. 

Along with this, the general lack of polish across things like voice acting and game physics, as well as the tedium behind upgrading the ship, makes Dreadmoor an easy title to stay away from, at least for now.
title: Dreadmoor Is a Dark Fishing Adventure That Doesn't Always Hook You [Early Access Review]

title: GTA 6 Gameplay - Our First Bank Robbery Went Horribly Wrong | A Day in Leonida #1

author: GamingBolt
description:
The scores are in, and wouldn't you know it, Grand Theft Auto 6 is amazing. Sorry, “universally acclaimed” and a “must-play.” It feels somewhat obvious – like this moment was predicted in time almost three years ago when the first trailer was revealed. But a 99 Metascore from 150+ critics feels unexpected. That something has finally, finally beaten that 28-year-long record set by the original Ocarina of Time on Metacritic makes it all the more auspicious. By several accounts, this is one of the greatest games of all time, and certainly of the year so far, which is saying something given the sheer competition.

Then again, it raises an important question and an inevitable comparison because, of course, it does. Plenty of “greatest games of all time” and more than enough Game of the Year winners have come along. However, looking at Rockstar Games, the one that comes to mind most readily is, of course, Red Dead Redemption 2. Even with all the machinations surrounding Red Dead Online, and
title: Why GTA 6 And Red Dead Redemption 2 Shouldn't Be Judged the Same Way
